h1: 华盛顿对华鹰派‘复仇’成功：黄仁勋出局，芯片出口管制要加码了？
category: 美国《华盛顿邮报》外刊讲解 第1229天
headline_en: Behind Jensen Huang's spy scandal, a shadow war for Trump's ear on China
headline_zh: 华盛顿对华鹰派‘复仇’成功：黄仁勋出局，芯片出口管制要加码了？
sources_note: 依据美国《华盛顿邮报》（The Washington Post）2026-11-15 报道。

paragraph_overrides.2: Huang’s downfall, which has the potential to mark a dramatic shift in power, was ultimately set in motion by one of the capital’s most influential China hard-liners, national security adviser and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Rubio issued a memo warning Trump about the relationship between Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, based on a report generated by the CIA, according to a person familiar with the matter. When the findings of Rubio’s memo — swiping at one of Trump’s closest allies — leaked in news reports, they set off a chain of events that culminated in Huang’s resignation Thursday.
paragraph_overrides.5: Many of Trump’s national security team had not shared the president’s view on exports of chips, according to a former official who worked on chips policy and is still connected to the industry, who likened Huang’s relationship to handing officials a “nuclear bomb.” “They wanted to destroy the influence Jensen had over the president,” said the former official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe internal dynamics. “Things are forever changed,” said Fedasiuk, a longtime advocate for controls on chip exports.
paragraph_overrides.6: For decades, Nvidia’s computer chips powered the graphics in video games and were not a matter of national security. But for many in Washington, that began to change at the start of the AI boom and what officials in the Biden administration saw as the dawn of a new contest with China poised to reshape the two nations’ military and economic power. Huang took a different view, arguing that chipmakers should be able to continue to sell into China, hooking them on American systems in a way that would ultimately benefit the U.S.
paragraph_overrides.8: Huang advocated for his position in sometimes caustic terms. In an interview with a podcast in September 2025, he said the term “China hawk” should be a badge of shame. “They think they’re doing the right thing for our country, but it’s not patriotic,” he said. “Not even a little bit.” Staff at Washington think tanks and on Capitol Hill responded by designing badges designating them China hawks that they passed around among themselves. At the time, Eric Sayers, a managing director at consulting firm Beacon Global Strategies, posted to social media that the group had “long memories” — a message he shared again in recent days as the scandal around Huang deepened.
paragraph_overrides.9: Now, with Huang sidelined — and Republican committee chairs planning to haul him in to provide information about the affair — the sponsors of a trio of new measures say they are increasingly optimistic that they can push them through as part of an annual defense bill. The bills would place export restrictions on the most powerful AI chips, require technology in chips to detect smuggling and limit Chinese access to chipmaking equipment. “Leading up to this moment, we were waiting to see who Nvidia deploys to kill these bills,” said a Senate Democratic aide, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe internal strategy. “Now all this stuff has come out, it puts them in a very, very tough position.
